nodes.label: Interface state
nodes.explanation: An admissible left/right interface state supplies acoustic/normal information and tangential receiving content. Trigger, output direction and spatial action must be interpreted separately.

nodes.label: Background PSD kernel
nodes.explanation: The background positive-semidefinite dissipation kernel acts directly on interface content. It is a separate pathway from the acoustically gated outputs.

nodes.label: Acoustic information
nodes.explanation: Acoustic / normal information constructs the acoustic trigger. Tangential receiving content does not construct this trigger.

nodes.label: Acoustic gate J
nodes.explanation: J is constructed from acoustic / normal information. delta_t (δ_t) DOES NOT ENTER THE GATE. Trigger ≠ Output: J may be nonzero even when tangential output is zero.

nodes.label: q_aa
nodes.explanation: The acoustically gated normal pathway routes dissipation to normal acoustic output; the gate is a trigger and does not by itself specify its receiving content.

nodes.label: Normal acoustic output
nodes.explanation: Normal acoustic output receives the q_aa pathway. Its direction and dissipative amplitude are distinct from the acoustic trigger.

nodes.label: q_at: OFF / ENABLED
nodes.explanation: OFF disables the cross-mode tangential pathway. ENABLED permits acoustic-triggered tangential action only when tangential receiving content is present; it does not alter the gate input.

nodes.label: Tangential receiving content
nodes.explanation: STRICT_1D: tangential jump = 0. WEAKLY_2D: tangential content may be nonzero with the same/similar acoustic trigger. delta_t is receiving content, not a gate input.

nodes.label: Tangential output
nodes.explanation: Actual dissipative amplitude depends on tangential receiving content as well as q_at and the acoustic trigger. In STRICT_1D, trigger may exist but cross-mode tangential output = 0 because tangential receiving content vanishes. In WEAKLY_2D, nonzero tangential content can activate the enabled q_at pathway.

nodes.label: Entropy-scaled combination
nodes.explanation: The background PSD kernel and the normal acoustic and tangential pathways combine in entropy-scaled coordinates as the selected positive-semidefinite dissipation operator. Combining output pathways does not add tangential receiving content to the acoustic gate input.

nodes.label: Physical entropy-variable dissipation
nodes.explanation: The combined operator is mapped to physical entropy variables and acts on the right-minus-left entropy-variable jump. The frozen production method applies this dissipative action with its entropy-conservative central flux. This schematic explains the mapping only; it evaluates no state, matrix or flux.

limitations.description: Authoritative five-epsilon Near-1D raw numerical evidence is missing. No epsilon slider, five-point numerical scan, formal Near-1D experiment or numeric chart is registered. Fig13 epsilon belongs to modal validation and cannot fill this gap.

For admissible near-one-dimensional states under the theoretical assumptions, cross-mode action is O(epsilon) and its entropy contribution is O(epsilon^2). This is a theoretical explanation, not a numerical fit or a measured five-epsilon scan.

The linked frozen Spectrum Evidence includes the production method source and its hash as implementation context. Its numerical spectra do not certify Near-1D asymptotic scaling. The schematic contains no J or dissipation values.
